quest.title: Home of the Hot Springs
quest.description: As the Pilgrimage draws to a close, Kachina emerges triumphant, and she joins the Night Warden Wars alongside some seasoned veterans. After the tournament, Mualani moots the idea of visiting the People of the Springs...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Primogem x30, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.title: Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn

talks.objective: Go to the People of the Springs

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're finally here! So, this is your home, Mualani! Paimon can't wait to have a look around!

dialogues.speaker: Moeava
dialogues.text: Ahh... See, what did I tell you? A dip in the hot springs after a battle is just the best!

dialogues.speaker: Taheta
dialogues.text: Fetch me a bottle of wine, would you, dear?

dialogues.speaker: Makemo
dialogues.text: Just one? Let's get another, it's still early in the day, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Taenga
dialogues.text: Wanna go to Golden Dusk later?

dialogues.speaker: Mersa
dialogues.text: Now this is a vacation... Absolutely amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's so lively around here! Is there some kind of holiday going on?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We try to treat every day like a holiday around here. We believe every day is worth celebrating.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Now, let me show you around. Hmm... where to start...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Xochicuicatl Records, Colomche Plaza... There are so many options, but I recommend starting with the real highlight around here.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: The hot springs, of course! Natural hot springs have tons of health benefits. Go for a nice, long soak, and you're guaranteed a good night's sleep!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Wait, you want us to bathe... here?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Oh, don't be shy. C'mon, I'll take you to get changed—
Mualani!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Huh? Oh... Auntie Atea!

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: Please, I've told you just "Atea" is fine. Do I look that old to you?

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: Were you taking these two to the hot springs?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: #That's right. Oh, let me introduce you. This is {NICKNAME}, and the small one next to {M#him}{F#her} is Paimon.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: They only just arrived in Natlan, so I'm taking them around to experience our customs!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hi, there!

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: Ah, I'm Mualani's neighbor, Atea. By the way, Mualani, I heard you lost to Kachina during the Pilgrimage. Is that true?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Yeah, I was THIS close to winning. *sigh*... Definitely not the result I wanted, but, still, not too surprising. Kachina's always been strong.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Anyway, it's all in the past. I'm gonna take these two for a dip in the hot springs. Talk to you later!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Oh, wait, you'll need swimsuits first... Hmm, I'm sure I can find something lying around the shop. I'll go look!

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: Hold it right there, young lady. Have you forgotten the rule about bathing in the hot springs?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Rule...? Oh, wait, you mean—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a rule about bathing in the hot springs?

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: That's right. Outlanders have to complete a "trial" at an artificial hot spring before they're allowed access to the natural ones.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: It's not nearly as scary as it sounds. Basically, natural hot springs have higher temperatures that not everyone can withstand.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: A few travelers have gotten scalded by the water in the past, so now we have an unwritten rule: All outlanders need to adapt to the lower-temperature, artificial springs first.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: But, seriously, Auntie Atea, do we have to be so strict? These two are formidable adventurers. I know they can handle it!

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: Famous last words... The hot springs are not to be underestimated. You can never be too careful. Besides, the environment's been unstable lately. It could be a sign that the Abyss is about to attack.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that sounds dangerous! Y'know, Paimon's really not all that "formidable," so... careful is good!

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: Exactly, there will be no excessive risk-taking on my watch. Mualani, take them to the artificial spring first.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Okay, okay.

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: That's more like it, and don't try anything funny. I'm heading to the artificial spring in a bit, and if I don't see you there... Your days of copping free meals at my place are done.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Relax, relax... Oh, by the way, Atea, how have you been feeling lately?

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: Much better — how else would I have the energy to keep an eye on all you rascals?

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: Hey, you over there! How many times have I told you, no roughhousing near the hot springs!

response.speaker: Niu
response.text: Oh, shoot, that weird lady's back again!

response.speaker: Anaa
response.text: Run!

response.speaker: Atea
response.text: Stop right there! You need a stern talking to!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She sure has a lot of energy...

choices.text: Is she an old friend of yours?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Haha, she's a legend in our tribe. Everyone knows her.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Back before I inherited my Ancient Name, she was one of Natlan's most renowned warriors, famous for her love of hot springs. In fact, she often threw parties at the hot springs.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: She referred to anyone who came to these parties as her "hot spring buddies." The attendees were all respected warriors like Liliuo, Kaiulani, Vichama... Oh, and the Archon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Paimon lived here, she would take advantage of the hot springs, too!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: It's just... During battle, she was impaled in the abdomen by an Abyssal monster.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: The doctors managed to save her life, but they made it clear that she could never bathe in the hot springs again.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Abyssal power still exists within her body. Immersing herself in hot water would accelerate the corrosion of her internal organs and the progression of her illness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, no wonder she had so many scars... Paimon had no idea she was so seriously injured...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: That's normal. She never talks about her injury.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: She's worked tirelessly over the years to dig up artificial springs so that more and more people can experience our tribe's natural wonders, even though she can't enjoy them herself. I really respect her for that.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Anyway, let's head to the artificial springs. If Auntie Atea gets there before us, we're gonna be in some real hot water.

choices.text: Do we have to fight something?

talks.objective: Head for the artificial hot springs

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Oh... I see. That's a great idea. I like it!

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: See, I told you the Chief would agree!

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: Let's get moving, then! We can't let a word of this slip to anyone else...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hey, Amina, Hikueru, Marokau! You three seem particularly cheerful today. What's the occasion?

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: Oh, Mualani, you're back! Umm, who are these two...?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #This is {NICKNAME} and Paimon, two very important guests. I wanted to take them to the natural hot springs, but Auntie Atea caught us, so we had to come here first.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Oh, what a coincidence! We were just talking about her.

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: We think Auntie Atea's illness has taken a turn for the better.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Really? How can you tell?

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: Okay, so, while you've been busy with the Pilgrimage, we noticed that she's been visiting the hot springs alone at night.

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: Specifically, the hot springs in the cave to the north of our settlement — I'm sure you know the one. Apparently, she used to go there a lot before they became abandoned for some reason.

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: She could never come into contact with hot water before, and now she's visiting the hot springs every night. I mean, it's pretty obvious what that means, right?

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: Yeah, so we got to thinking... What if we renovated the abandoned spring behind her back, then threw her a huge surprise party!

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: Chief Amina thinks it's a great idea, too. So, you want in?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Of course! How could you even think of pulling this off without me?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I'm a little busy right now, though. I'll come find you once we're done at the hot springs.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Of course, take your time! You should focus on our guests, for now.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: These artificial springs are pretty new, but the experience is just as good as the natural ones, if you ask me. We really worked hard on them, so I hope you enjoy!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: And you two... I know you want to focus on Atea's surprise, but don't forget your patrol duties in the meantime. The Abyss could attack at any moment, so we need to stay vigilant.

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: You got it, Chief. We'll keep an eye out — you can count on us.

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: Alright, we're off, then. See you at the abandoned spring, Mualani.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I'm also gonna head out. Have fun!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Finally, it's hot spring time! Oh, I already arranged swimwear for you guys, by the way. C'mon, I'll show you to the changing room.

talks.objective: Try the artificial hot springs out

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wait, why does it fit surprisingly well...?)

talks.objective: Change into the outfit Mualani prepared

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Wait, why does it fit surprisingly well...?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahhh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oooph... So, what do you think? Can you feel the warmth relax every muscle in your body?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's so nice. The steam is warm too...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: The first time I came to the hot springs, there was no calming effect whatsoever. I was such a little ball of energy, the moment my parents looked away, I ran off to the high-temperature pools.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: It's actually pretty funny looking back on it. They were absolutely frantic, looking for me all over, until, finally, they saw my head slowly poke out from under the water.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I was too young to remember the whole ordeal, but my parents told me all about it. A natural-born swimmer, my mother called me. Just like her, I taught myself how to dive underwater the first time I ever went swimming.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: So, feel free to go for a swim. I'll be right here if you need rescuing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, here goes nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Ahem.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Auntie Atea! You really came to check on us?

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Of course, and I'm glad you listened. I brought you all some milk and snacks as well — I'll just leave them here.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: The temperature in the artificial springs isn't too high, so I went with Saurus Crackers and Grainfruit Chips. See how you like them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mmm, these are great!

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Well, I did make them myself.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Very few young people know how to truly appreciate hot springs, so listen carefully. The temperature of the hot spring not only determines the types of snacks you should choose, but also the amount of time you should spend in the water.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: To bathe in a hot spring is to completely empty your mind. As such, swimming around the pool is incredibly disruptive and impolite... and something you should absolutely not learn from Mualani.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hey!

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Alright. Looks like you were able to adapt to the temperature no problem. You should be able to switch to the natural springs, then.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Well, I've got to get going. Oh, and make sure you drink your milk. I'm looking at you, Mualani. I still remember how you used to pour it into the water when you were little.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: That better not happen again, whether I'm here to catch you or not.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Okay, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't think you were the type to do something like that...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Haha, I remember thinking I'd totally get away with it, too! But, turns out milk is pretty easy to spot when you pour it into clear water... Not my best work.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You drink the milk and enjoy the hot spring with Mualani...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Some people get dizzy if they stay in here too long. You guys alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's fine, just a bit stuffed...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I feel fine, too.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Looks like you two are naturals! Oh, by the way, I have to leave you on your own for a little while this afternoon. I'm gonna help the others fix up that abandoned spring.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I certainly don't trust their aesthetic tastes. Who knows what will become of the place if I leave them unattended?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: In exchange, though, I can recommend a couple of shops that are worth a visit...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Atea has been really kind to us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! She brought us snacks and taught us about the hot springs... We wanna do our part too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Friends are supposed to help each other out! We'd feel bad, otherwise.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Well, then... The more the merrier!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Alright, we should get going. Let's organize the best hot spring gathering Natlan's ever seen!

choices.text: As long as we're not in the way...

talks.objective: Meet up with Marokau and the others

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: Mualani! Wait, you brought our guests, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here to help!

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: But, you're important guests! We can't put you to work!

choices.text: We want to do our part.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Alright, alright. Stop trying to out-polite each other, would you? The sooner we get this party started the sooner we get to enjoy the real party!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Now, where to start... Hmm, looks like the water outlet is blocked pretty bad. We'll need to dig under it.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Those boxes in the corner need to be thrown out as well... Gah. They're moldy as all get out!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Also, someone needs to go out and get some cloth, wood, and decorations... Oh, and snacks, too! I say we get enough for twenty or thirty people. Bulk purchases fetch the best prices, after all... Oh, but don't just accept the first offer they give you—

response.speaker: Hikueru
response.text: Um... I'm not good at haggling. Why don't you go?

response.speaker: Marokau
response.text: Hey, I'm not any better, and I wouldn't even know what to buy. Umm, how about we handle things here while you three deal with the shopping?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Yeah, that works, too!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I can introduce you to all the shops while we're at it. Alright, let's meet back here later.

choices.text: We don't have anything else to do at the moment.

talks.objective: Go to the market street to buy the necessary goods

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hey there, Yelafath. Hope business has been going well.

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Well, if it isn't Mualani. Back from the Pilgrimage?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's right. Didn't make the cut this year, though.

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Well, it wouldn't be a competition if everyone got to win. So, what'll it be today?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Here, it's all on the list — quite a sizeable order, as you can see. So, uh... can we expect a discount?

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Wow, that is large order. What's it all for, a party?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's right. Keep this between us for now... but, we're throwing a hot spring party for Auntie Atea.

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Wait, you're saying she can go in the hot springs again? That's great news! How about this — you can have the decorations on the house, and I'll give you twenty percent off the cloth and wood.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: C'mon, I know you can sweeten the deal. That pile of wood's been sitting there since I left for the Pilgrimage. At this rate, you need to get rid of it or it's gonna go moldy...

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Alright, alright... *sigh* Such a handful. Just give me a moment while I pack all this up for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that was amazing, Mualani!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Haha, all in a day's work. By the way, Yelafath, are these two stones for sale?

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Interested? They won't come cheap.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I'm not planning to haggle this time, I promise. Package them separately, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are those also decorations?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Nope. Kachina likes shiny little trinkets, so whenever I come across something like that, I always buy it for her.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I'll hold onto them for now. It'll be a nice, little surprise for her when she returns victorious from battle. I'm sure she'll like it.

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Alright, that should be everything. If you could just double-check — make sure nothing's missing.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Lemme see... Huh? What's this crate of juice doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: That's on the house.

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: Seven years ago, when the Abyss attacked our tribe, Atea saved my brother's life. She never asked for anything in return, but I could never forget what she did for my family that day.

dialogues.speaker: Yelafath
dialogues.text: So, send her my regards, would you? And have fun!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh, we will! It's gonna be a party to remember! Thanks a lot, Yelafath!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Well, that's our shopping done. Let's head back.

talks.objective: Return to the abandoned hot spring

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We're back. How's everything going?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Wow, this place cleaned up nice! You got the water unblocked, too! Good work.

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: I would hope so. We spent all day clearing out debris from the bottom of the spring.

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: Did you guys get everything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we brought back tons of stuff. We set it down near the cave entrance.

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: Alright, then, roll up your sleeves, everyone, and let's get back to work!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Actually, why don't you two take a break. I'll handle it from here. {NICKNAME}, mind lending me a hand?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: So, I was brainstorming on the way over, and I'm thinking we could draw something on the wall over here, and the snacks and drinks can go over there...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Under Mualani's direction, you give the abandoned spring a new look...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: So, what do you think? Not bad, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It looks amazing! Paimon had no idea you were such a great designer!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Well, I'm usually the one in charge of the family store, so I'm pretty good at things like renovation and organization.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Not to mention, this was totally a group effort... Still, I didn't expect it to take quite this long... Guess it's too late to invite Auntie Atea over, huh...

response.speaker: Hikueru
response.text: Yeah, tonight's definitely not gonna work. Chief Amina set up those patrols to guard against the Abyss, and Atea volunteered. So, she's on watch tonight.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I see. Well, guess the surprise will have to wait until tomorrow.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hmm... This could actually be a good thing. She can relieve all the exhaustion of keeping watch all night by soaking in the hot spring! She's gonna love it!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: #Well, let's call it a day, then! {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you must be tired, too. C'mon, I'll take you to the inn.

talks.objective: Return to the inn to rest

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Alright, this is it. Get a good night's sleep, okay? I'll see you tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! Goodnight!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn*... Paimon's exhausted. We really went all over the place today, didn't we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, we need to be well-rested for the party tomorrow, so let's head inside!

talks.objective: Go back to the inn and sleep
Deal with the unforeseen situation

dialogues.text: To arms, everyone! To arms!
Ugh, why now!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *snore*... Huh? What's with all the noise...?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, wake up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mualani? What's going on... Ahhh, where did all these monsters come from!?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: It's the Abyss. Our patrols are trying to drive them back as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Come with me. I'll take you somewhere safe!

dialogues.speaker: Taheta
dialogues.text: Mualani, a little help over here? We can't hold 'em back much longer!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: One moment. I'll be right there!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Really? That's perfect! I've been waiting for the chance to fight by your side!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hang in there, we're here to help!

choices.text: Let's show those creatures what we're made of.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Couldn't have said it better myself!

talks.objective: Repel the Abyss incursion
Talk to Mualani

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We've cleared out most of the monsters over here. Thanks for your help — it would've taken me ages on my own.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Looks like we're still in for a long night, though. We still have no idea where these creatures are coming from...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Let's go ask Amina. She'll have a better handle on the situation.

talks.objective: Go with Mualani to find Amina

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Amina!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Oh, It's you three... Thank you for helping clear out all those monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: We were prepared for an attack, but we didn't have enough people to prevent them from breaking through our defenses. No casualties so far, though.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Where'd they come from this time?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: The east side. We've pinpointed the position of an Abyssal Pylon, but we don't have enough manpower to take it down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: An Abyssal Pylon? What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: A kind of "gate" created by the Abyss, one that allows monsters from the Night Kingdom to enter the physical world.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: The only way to end the attack is to destroy the Pylon as soon as possible. Otherwise, the endless hordes of monsters will exhaust our defenses.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Exactly, that's what I'm most concerned about. Their numbers suggest there might even be multiple Pylons in the area. We're searching for them as we speak...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Alright, we'll go seal off the one to the east. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, can I count on your help again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! We can't just sit back and do nothing!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: On behalf of the People of the Springs, you have my thanks. We're counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Let's go, there's no time to lose. Take care, Amina.

talks.objective: Destroy the Abyssal Pylon
Talk to Mualani

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, that should do it, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I don't see any more monsters, so looks like we're in the clear.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do these attacks happen a lot? Must be hard on your tribe...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yeah, it makes things hard sometimes, but that's how our ancestors have always lived.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Besides, the Abyss doesn't care how difficult our lives are. Fighting back is the only option.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: C'mon, we should head back... Huh? What are you looking at? Is there something over there?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right! Mualani, look! They're coming from that direction!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, that area looks kinda familiar...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's the location of the abandoned spring!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Wh—What!? How unlucky can we get? We just finished the renovations!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: We probably don't have any reinforcements over there, so it's up to us! Let's move!

talks.objective: Go to the abandoned hot spring

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Atea! What are you doing here? Where's the Pylon?

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Hah, where do you think...? If I'm here, means that thing is long gone.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: I was in a hurry, so it's not my best work. You should check if all the important stuff is still here.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Stop talking for now. That wound looks bad... The Abyssal power is corroding your body.

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: Is this the right area? Hello? Anyone there?

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: Mualani! And... Atea? What's going on? We were told the second Pylon was over here...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Atea took care of it, but she's injured... Quick, someone get a doctor!

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, stop fussing. Don't you think I know my own limits? The main thing is, they didn't destroy anything. This is a beautiful hot spring, by the way. I can tell how much work you put into it.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Wait, no. This was meant to be... a surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: For me, right? I know.

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: Atea...

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: You think I couldn't tell you were avoiding me on purpose? Not one of you stopped to say hello today... It couldn't be more obvious that you were hiding something.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: And you, Mualani. Were you the one that bought the snacks? How many times have I told you? You have to choose them based on the temperature of the water...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh, forget about that. The doctor's almost here, and you're gonna get all better. Then, we can have a meal together, and I'll help you make whatever you want, okay? You just have to hold on...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Mualani said Atea had been injured by the Abyss before. Maybe that's why the corrosion is so fast this time...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (At this rate, she's not going to make it until help arrives. Maybe there's something I can do.)

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: The impurities and the elemental energy we embody repel each other.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? The crystal has been purified!? When?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The anguish he feels... has brought him to tears...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I also came across a Teardrop Crystal. Can you purify it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That's right. Back then, I...)

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Atea? Atea!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me try something...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Wait, what do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: What is this? Some sort of purification? The Abyssal power... It's being cleansed away!

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: How can that be!?

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: I never knew that was even possible...

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Atea!

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: The mark of the Abyss... It's gone...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Yes, thanks to {NICKNAME}... By the way, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I just saw you purify Abyssal power from Atea's body. That didn't injure you in any way, did it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You're sure?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Good, good...

response.speaker: Hikueru
response.text: Thank goodness!

response.speaker: Marokau
response.text: You scared us all half to death just now!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: A group of young tribespeople race over to surround you and Atea.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: They toss you into the air over and over, as if welcoming a triumphant hero.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Alright, everyone, head back and get some rest. We'll meet here tomorrow!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: We'll celebrate Atea's recovery, and our triumph over the Abyss!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: #And most importantly, we'll show {NICKNAME} and Paimon how grateful we are for their aid. Let's make it an occasion to remember! Dismissed!

response.speaker: Crowd
response.text: Got it!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Got any other secret powers I should know about, haha? But, seriously, you really came through for us tonight, so thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon almost forgot you had that ability. You used it back in Mondstadt to cleanse Dvalin's tears, didn't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That was some quick thinking, {NICKNAME}... Huh? You look like something's bothering you. What's wrong?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I didn't want to spoil the mood earlier, but when I was purifying the Abyssal power within Atea, I could sense something...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Remnants of that power have existed within her body for years, corroding it from the inside...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I did my best to cleanse that power just now, but it's already deeply ingrained within her internal organs, leaving her as fragile as a dried leaf in the wind.)

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Abyssal power still exists within her body. Immersing herself in hot water would accelerate the corrosion of her internal organs and the progression of her illness.

response.speaker: Marokau
response.text: We think Auntie Atea's illness has taken a turn for the better.

response.speaker: Hikueru
response.text: She could never come into contact with hot water before, and now she's visiting the hot springs every night. I mean, it's pretty obvious what that means, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I don't think she was going to the hot springs because she was recovering, but because she realized her condition had taken a decisive turn for the worse... I'm just not sure if I should tell Mualani.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hellooo! {NICKNAME}! Maybe you can zone out some other time, because Paimon can barely keep her eyes open. Let's head back for now.

talks.objective: Take part in the hot springs party

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Not interested in hanging out with the other kids?

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Snacks not to your taste? Hot spring temperature too high?

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: ...None of the above, huh? I heard you were the one who cleansed the Abyssal power yesterday... You sensed it, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: *sigh* I was hoping to keep it a secret for a few more days, didn't want to ruin the celebrations and all, but looks like it was no use... Hey, kid!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Who, me?

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Yes, you. C'mon, let's go for a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: Hey, where are you going? Did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Just going to get some air. It's too noisy in here.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: You have fun — we'll be right back. Oh, and there are extra snacks in that box over there if they need replenishing. Baked them all fresh this the morning.

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: Alright! Sounds great!

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Mualani.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yeah?

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: ...You've gotten so tall, you know that? Feels like just yesterday you were that rambunctious kid, causing trouble all around the hot springs. It's like all that time passed by in the blink of an eye...

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Tell me, how are your parents?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: They're away on business... Seriously, Atea, what's going on? You're acting strange...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, did something happen? Both of you seem a little off today...

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: I guess I should explain.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: I wasn't visiting the hot springs because I was getting better. And that Pylon yesterday... I didn't go face it by myself because I was reckless, or too anxious to wait for reinforcements...

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: It's because my body isn't going to last much longer.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Your friend saved my life in that cave, and because of that, I got to enjoy this celebration with you all... But, I'm just a few days shy of the end.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: The hot springs... I'm just trying to enjoy them for as long as I have left.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Mualani?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: "That better not happen again, whether I'm here to catch you or not" — that's what you said back at the artificial spring. I... had a bad feeling then, but I didn't want it to be true.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I... wanted to believe you were actually recovering...

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: You wanna know something? Recovery, death... To me, the two aren't all that different. Both are worth celebrating.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: You've never been resurrected, so you might not understand, but death and I? We're old pals by now. There's nothing sad about being reunited with an old friend.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: I lived with regret for a long time... regret that my illness meant I could no longer take to the frontlines, especially as our nation slid deeper into crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: But, yesterday, I was finally able to let go of that regret. Not only because I found the strength to fight the Abyss, even at the end of my life... But because I got to see you in action, Mualani.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Seeing you out there... It made me realize that I don't need to worry about our tribe or our nation's future. You have the capacity to bring us all together.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Even if I was never injured, old age would still take me one day, but I've done what I needed to do — the future is in your hands now.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Just remember — whether in life or death, I am always with you.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I understand. Seems like you've given this a lot of thought, Atea. Thank you for telling me all this.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I'll do everything in my power to protect our tribe, our nation, and live up to the example you set for me.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Good... Oh, and, if any of you have the chance to meet with the Archon, could you give this to her for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: A talisman I've carried with me my whole life. It may seem strange to say while I'm still alive, but just think of it as a "relic" I'm leaving for her.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: It's brought me good fortune in battle. Even after I became too sick to fight, I never took it off.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Just tell her it "embodies fond memories and my strength of will." She'll know what I'm trying to say.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't worry... We'll make sure she gets it.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Alright, that's all I wanted to say. Let's head back to the party. No use spending what little time I have left being sad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Atea, Mualani! If you don't hurry up, there won't be any snacks left!

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Excuse me, what did I say about bathing in the hot springs on a full stomach? Hey, are you listening to me—

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone has a great time amid the festive atmosphere. When it comes time to go, Atea says goodbye with a smile.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: When she reaches your group, she pats Mualani on the shoulder lightly.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: "Life is a journey in which there's no turning back, so forge ahead and don't hold back."

talks.objective: Additional
Additional

dialogues.speaker: Hikueru
dialogues.text: To digging, then?

dialogues.speaker: Marokau
dialogues.text: Let's go!

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are your plans, Kinich?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I've gotta deliver some ceremonial artifacts back to my tribe. I didn't place too well in this Pilgrimage, so, now that it's over, it's time to get home and get back to work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You didn't get enough points?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yeah. I got injured during the team round and wound up losing two key matches during individual competition — both against opponents I'd faced many times in the past. We've each had our fair share of wins and losses. It happens.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Haha, that's what you get for locking me away earlier! Get used to the taste of karma... May those injuries be the first of many!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: ...Hey! What are you doing!? Argh...!

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Phew... Thank you for your help. The Abyss has fled back to the Night Kingdom, and the water temperature's back to normal.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Guess that means we've got multiple things to celebrate at this party!

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With doubts still lingering in your heart, you return to the inn to rest until the next morning. Until it's time for the hot spring party...

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mualani, is that the Pylon?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's it, alright. C'mon, let's get rid of this thing!

dialogues.speaker: Taenga
dialogues.text: Huh? Seems like the monsters are decreasing in number...

dialogues.speaker: Tureia
dialogues.text: C'mon, everyone! Keep it up!
